summary: Aminophylline is the ethylenediamine salt of theophylline (roughly 80% theophylline by weight), a methylxanthine bronchodilator. Intravenous theophylline is indicated as an adjunct to inhaled beta-2 agonists and systemic corticosteroids for acute exacerbations of reversible airflow obstruction in asthma, emphysema and chronic bronchitis. It is a narrow-therapeutic-index drug: dosing must be individualized to serum theophylline concentration (target 10-20 mcg/mL), because clearance varies up to fourfold between similar patients and is altered by age, concurrent illness (heart failure, liver disease, fever, sepsis), smoking, and many drug interactions. Toxicity (vomiting, arrhythmias, seizures) can be life-threatening, particularly with chronic overdosage.
indications: Adjunct to inhaled beta-2 selective agonists and systemic corticosteroids for treatment of acute exacerbations of symptoms and reversible airflow obstruction in asthma
Treatment of reversible airflow obstruction in other chronic lung diseases such as emphysema and chronic bronchitis

dosage.n: If patient already received theophylline, obtain a serum level first and calculate loading dose from the deficit

dosage.n: Individualize entirely on serum theophylline concentration; reduce in heart failure, liver disease, fever, sepsis, elderly

admin: Administer intravenously; give loading dose slowly over 30 minutes to avoid arrhythmia/hypotension
Use ideal (lean) body weight for dose calculations
Do not give a loading dose if any theophylline was taken in the previous 24 hours without first measuring a serum level
Measure serum theophylline 30 minutes after a loading dose to guide further dosing
Monitor serum theophylline frequently (e.g., every 24 h) in acutely ill patients and when clearance may change
Dilute and infuse per product instructions; do not give rapid IV bolus
moa: Theophylline relaxes airway smooth muscle (bronchodilation) and suppresses airway responsiveness to stimuli. Bronchodilation is mediated chiefly by inhibition of phosphodiesterase isoenzymes (PDE III and to a lesser extent PDE IV), raising cyclic AMP; non-bronchodilator prophylactic effects involve other mechanisms. Adenosine receptor antagonism and PDE III inhibition also account for several adverse effects (tachycardia, arrhythmia, headache, emesis). Theophylline additionally increases diaphragmatic contractility via adenosine-mediated calcium uptake. Bronchodilation occurs over a serum concentration of about 5-20 mcg/mL.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to theophylline or other components, including ethylenediamine
relative: Conditions reducing theophylline clearance (heart failure, cor pulmonale, liver disease, sepsis, sustained fever, hypothyroidism)
monitor: Symptoms of toxicity (nausea, vomiting, tremor, agitation)

preg: There are no adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Not shown to be teratogenic in mice or rats, but embryotoxic in rats at high maternal doses. Theophylline clearance changes in the third trimester. Use only if the benefit justifies the potential risk and monitor serum concentrations.
lact: Theophylline is excreted into breast milk at concentrations roughly equal to maternal serum and may cause irritability or signs of mild toxicity in the nursing infant. Serious effects are unlikely unless maternal serum levels are toxic; monitor the infant.
renal: Renal impairment has little effect on clearance in adults, but reduces clearance in infants under 3 months of age. Guide dosing by serum theophylline concentration.
hepatic: Theophylline clearance is markedly reduced in cirrhosis and acute hepatitis - reduce the dose, monitor serum levels frequently, and watch closely for toxicity.

major: CYP1A2/CYP3A4 inhibitors (cimetidine, ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolones, erythromycin/clarithromycin, fluvoxamine, tacrine, allopurinol high-dose, propranolol) - reduce clearance and raise theophylline to toxic levels
Enzyme inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St John's wort, smoking) - increase clearance and lower theophylline levels
Ephedrine / sympathomimetics and other xanthines - additive CNS and cardiac stimulation/toxicity
moderate: Lithium - theophylline increases renal lithium clearance, lowering lithium levels
minor: Influenza vaccine, interferon - may transiently reduce clearance
interactions.food: Large amounts of caffeine/xanthine-containing foods or beverages add to stimulant effects; charcoal-broiled (high-protein/low-carbohydrate) diets can increase clearance.
interactions.alcohol: Acute alcohol ingestion can reduce theophylline clearance and raise serum levels.
interactions.diagnostics: Caffeine and other xanthines may interfere with theophylline assays; theophylline can cause transient diuresis and mild hyperglycemia.

serious: Cardiac arrhythmias (including multifocal atrial tachycardia, ventricular arrhythmias)
Seizures (can be intractable at high levels)
rare: Hypersensitivity to ethylenediamine component (rash, exfoliative dermatitis)
Seizures at levels under 20 mcg/mL in patients with neurological disease or the elderly
emergency: Severe hypotension or cardiac arrest from rapid IV bolus

monitoring: Serum theophylline concentration (therapeutic target 10-20 mcg/mL); measure 30 min after loading dose and frequently in acute illness
Serum potassium and glucose (especially in overdose)
Clinical signs of toxicity - nausea, vomiting, tremor, agitation, seizures
Re-assess dose after changes in smoking status, intercurrent illness, or interacting drugs
counsel: This is a strong bronchodilator with a narrow safe range - blood levels will be checked
Report nausea, vomiting, palpitations, tremor, agitation, or seizures promptly
Tell your doctor before starting or stopping smoking, or any new medicine, as it can change your blood level
Limit caffeine-containing drinks and avoid extra over-the-counter stimulants
Take oral forms consistently; do not double up if a dose is missed
pk: Rapid after IV loading dose; bronchodilation over serum 5-20 mcg/mL
Post-distribution serum level ~30 min after a 30-min IV loading infusion
Highly variable: ~8 h healthy non-smoking adults; shorter in smokers/children, much longer (>24 h) in cirrhosis, heart failure, neonates
Maintained by continuous infusion; volume of distribution ~0.5 L/kg
Store per product labeling at controlled room temperature; protect from light and freezing
pearls: Narrow therapeutic index - ALWAYS dose to serum theophylline level (target 10-20 mcg/mL), never to a fixed mg/kg alone
Aminophylline is about 80% theophylline by weight - 5.7 mg/kg aminophylline equals ~4.6 mg/kg theophylline
Many drugs (ciprofloxacin, cimetidine, erythromycin, fluvoxamine) sharply raise levels - check for interactions before starting
Reduce dose and monitor closely in heart failure, liver disease, sepsis, sustained fever, hypothyroidism and the elderly
Chronic overdosage causes seizures and arrhythmias at lower peak levels than acute overdosage - falsely 'normal' levels can still be dangerous
missed: For maintenance oral therapy, take a missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not double the dose. For intravenous infusions, dosing is managed by the clinical team and titrated to serum levels.
overdose: Theophylline overdose can be life-threatening. Acute overdose (<24 h) may cause vomiting, tachyarrhythmia, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia and seizures (seizures more likely above ~100 mcg/mL); chronic overdosage causes seizures and arrhythmias at lower levels. Manage with supportive care, cardiac and serum level monitoring, control of seizures (benzodiazepines) and arrhythmias, correction of hypokalemia, multiple-dose activated charcoal, and hemodialysis/charcoal hemoperfusion for severe toxicity or very high levels.
